description: Team store ops (spec/schema/README.md, Teams; design sections 4.5-4.14). Each vector names a world: every team log (thread and branch ids and its events, prev_hash left out: a runner seeds them under its own header and chains them) and the index rows those logs rebuild (team_feed left out). Worlds share most events and rows, so each is stored once, in events and rows, and a world names it by id (the first 16 hex digits of the sha256 of its RFC 8785 bytes). The runner seeds the world, runs op as the writer of log `by` with `input` at clock `now` (and the limits in `given`), then compares the op's outcome, the event types it appended per log, in order (none for a log not listed), and the row changes per table: rows inserted, rows updated (as they are after), and the keys of rows deleted. Every appended event also adds its team_feed row. Claims are off. Ops: start, send, ask, reply, cancel, wait, monitor (a model call: input.call_id and input.args of a pending tool_call; or an operator request in the team log: request_id, principal, body, idempotency_key?), consume, deadline (the worker's step for input.id, an AskId or WaitId), materialize (input.rebind is what the rebind found), idle and end (the member's own settling appends).

vectors.name: send-lead-to-member
vectors.description: The lead sends a running member a message: the team's grant, message_sent (kind message, to researcher-1 at generation 1, the lead's run as provenance, the call as causal) and the call's result; the mail row is pending.

vectors.name: send-unknown-member-refused
vectors.description: No member has that name: the decision is logged, then the refusal as the result.

vectors.name: send-self-refused
vectors.description: The lead addresses itself: refused self.

vectors.name: send-member-ended-refused
vectors.description: The member ended (its rebind failed): refused member_ended.

vectors.name: send-mailbox-full-refused
vectors.description: A starting member's pending task already fills a mailbox of 1: refused mailbox_full.

vectors.name: send-member-to-lead
vectors.description: A member sends the lead a message; its provenance is its task's (the lead's run).

vectors.name: send-team-closed-refused
vectors.description: The lead ended, which closed the team (teams.closed_at) and sent the researcher a cancel it hasn't applied yet; the researcher's send is refused team_closed.

vectors.name: send-operator
vectors.description: team.send with an idempotency key: operator_request (its own event is the root request), the team's grant, and message_sent from {operator: request_id}; the mail row and the operator_receipts row are inserted.

vectors.name: send-operator-member-ended-refused
vectors.description: team.send to an ended member: the request, the grant and operator_refused.

vectors.name: send-operator-other-tenant-forbidden
vectors.description: An operator acting for a principal of another tenant: default deny, logged, then operator_refused{forbidden}.

vectors.name: ask-member-opens
vectors.description: writer-1 asks researcher-1: the grant, message_sent{ask} whose ask_id is its mail_id and whose deadline is now plus the default 120 s, then the park on the ask. It is the writer's first park while the lead's task monitor on it is unfired, so the same append sends the lead the one member_parked notice. The asks row is open.

vectors.name: ask-budget-exceeded
vectors.description: No headroom on a budget covering the recipient: refused budget_exceeded, after the send checks.

vectors.name: ask-operator-opens
vectors.description: team.ask with a 60 s timeout: operator_request, the grant and message_sent{ask} with deadline now + 60 s. The team log parks nothing.

vectors.name: reply-sent
vectors.description: The researcher replies to the ask it received: message_sent{reply} to the asker, with the ask's provenance, and the call's result. No policy decision.

vectors.name: reply-unknown-ask-refused
vectors.description: No ask with that id reached this log. The refusal is the call's result; nothing is sent.

vectors.name: reply-already-replied-refused
vectors.description: This log already replied to the ask. The refusal is the call's result; nothing is sent.

vectors.name: reply-past-deadline-refused
vectors.description: The asks row is still open, but now is its deadline: refused ask_closed. The refusal is the call's result; nothing is sent.

vectors.name: reply-ask-closed-refused
vectors.description: The asker's deadline step already closed the ask timed_out. The refusal is the call's result; nothing is sent.

vectors.name: ask-reply-closes-ask
vectors.description: The parked writer takes the reply as control mail: message_received, ask_closed {answered}, resumed and the ask call's one result, in one append.

vectors.name: ask-bounce-closes-member-ended
vectors.description: The writer asked the starting researcher, whose rebind then failed: the ask's bounce carries its ask_id and the result, and the parked writer closes the ask member_ended.

vectors.name: ask-deadline-timed-out
vectors.description: The team worker's deadline step at the deadline, with no reply or bounce pending: ask_closed{timed_out}, resumed and the call's result.

vectors.name: ask-deadline-reply-wins
vectors.description: At the deadline a reply is pending: it committed while the ask was open and before the deadline, so the step answers, never times out.

vectors.name: ask-deadline-not-due
vectors.description: Before the deadline the step does nothing.

vectors.name: ask-operator-reply-closes-ask
vectors.description: team.ask's reply reaches the team log, which takes everything: message_received and ask_closed{answered}; no resumed and no tool_result (team.ask returns it).

vectors.name: ask-deadline-cancel-pending
vectors.description: At the deadline the writer's cancel is pending and no reply or bounce is: the step applies the cancel (receipt and barrier), which closes the ask cancelled, not timed_out.

vectors.name: ask-operator-deadline-team-closed
vectors.description: The lead ended, which closed the team, while the operator's ask was open. Team close is a trigger of its own: the team log's next step closes the ask cancelled at once, long before its deadline (no resumed and no result: team.ask returns it).

vectors.name: cancel-requested
vectors.description: The lead cancels the member it started: the grant, message_sent{cancel} and cancel_requested as the result. Durable, not yet applied.

vectors.name: cancel-not-starter-forbidden
vectors.description: writer-1 did not start researcher-1: default deny, logged, and refused forbidden.

vectors.name: cancel-member-ended-refused
vectors.description: The member already ended: refused member_ended.

vectors.name: cancel-operator
vectors.description: team.cancel: operator_request, the grant and message_sent{cancel}.

vectors.name: consume-message-opens-idle-member
vectors.description: The idle researcher's one pending message is taken: message_received copies the whole envelope, opens a turn and the row becomes running.

vectors.name: consume-batch-shares-one-request
vectors.description: Two pending messages of different requests (the operator's, created first, and the lead's run): the batch is the longest prefix sharing the first row's principal and root request, so only the operator's is taken; the lead's stays pending for a later turn.

vectors.name: consume-mid-turn-takes-its-request
vectors.description: The researcher is mid-turn on the lead's run: only the row of that run is taken, and the operator's (created first) stays pending.

vectors.name: consume-parked-leaves-ordinary-mail
vectors.description: The writer is parked on its ask: the lead's ordinary message stays pending.

vectors.name: consume-nothing-pending
vectors.description: Nothing is addressed to the researcher.

vectors.name: consume-member-parked-parks-lead
vectors.description: writer-1, which the idle lead started, parked on an ask; its one member_parked notice is control mail: the lead's task monitor row still exists, so message_received and parked{kind: member} in one append. No turn opens.

vectors.name: consume-member-parked-after-settle
vectors.description: The writer parked, then settled before the lead consumed anything. The member_parked notice finds its task monitor row gone (the settlement deleted it): receipt only. The settlement is then ordinary mail and opens the idle lead's turn.

vectors.name: consume-settle-resolves-member-park
vectors.description: The lead is parked on writer-1 ({kind: member}); the writer's settlement is control mail: message_received then resumed, which clears the last park and opens the turn.

vectors.name: cancel-applied-running-member
vectors.description: The researcher's writer takes the cancel mail at a step boundary: message_received and today's barrier, cancel_requested{scope: tree}, with actor {host, provenance.principal}. The barrier rules then end the member cancelled.

vectors.name: cancel-applied-parked-asker
vectors.description: Cancel mail is control mail, taken while the writer is parked on its ask: the receipt, the barrier, and the ask closed cancelled with resumed and the call's result.

vectors.name: consume-unparked-mail-waits
vectors.description: The lead is parked on writer-1, whose settlement is pending, and so is an operator message of another request. The settlement is control mail: receipt and resumed, which opens the lead's turn under the lead's run. The operator's message is ordinary mail that the control row unblocked: it waits for the next consume, so one turn never holds two authorities.

vectors.name: cancel-applied-asker-with-pending-reply
vectors.description: The cancel mail is ahead of a reply the researcher sent while the ask was open. ask.complete's order still holds: the reply wins, so the ask closes answered, and the barrier follows the cancel's receipt.

vectors.name: cancel-applied-waiter
vectors.description: writer-1 is parked on a wait when its cancel is applied: the receipt, the barrier, and the wait finishes with what has settled (nothing, so timed_out: the mode is unmet), which deletes its settle monitor row; resumed and the wait call's result follow.

vectors.name: cancel-applied-waiter-counts-committed-settlement-cancel-first
vectors.description: writer-1 waits on researcher-1. Its cancel and the researcher's settlement are both committed before the writer consumes, the cancel first. Either way the settlement counts (commit order, as at the deadline step): applying the cancel consumes the wait's committed notices, then finishes the wait with the researcher in finished and timed_out false.

vectors.name: cancel-applied-waiter-counts-committed-settlement-settlement-first
vectors.description: writer-1 waits on researcher-1. Its cancel and the researcher's settlement are both committed before the writer consumes, the settlement first. Either way the settlement counts (commit order, as at the deadline step): applying the cancel consumes the wait's committed notices, then finishes the wait with the researcher in finished and timed_out false.

vectors.name: cancel-stops-new-work
vectors.description: The idle researcher's pending mail is the lead's cancel, then a message of the same run. The cancel is applied, and a cancelled member takes no new work: the message stays pending (the member's end refuses it), so no turn opens.

vectors.name: start-lead-starts
vectors.description: The lead starts a second researcher: its name is researcher-2 (k counts that agent's members, read in the transaction). member_started (its parent is itself, through the lead) and the task's message_sent insert the starting row, the pending task and the lead's task monitor; the call's result says started.

vectors.name: start-names-after-ended
vectors.description: researcher-1 ended; a new start is still researcher-2: an ended member keeps its name.

vectors.name: start-member-forbidden
vectors.description: Only a lead starts: writer-1's start is denied by default, logged, and refused.

vectors.name: start-unknown-agent
vectors.description: The team lists no such agent.

vectors.name: start-concurrency-cap
vectors.description: teamLimits.concurrent is 1 and researcher-1 is running: starting and running members count toward the cap, idle and ended ones don't.

vectors.name: start-budget-exceeded
vectors.description: No headroom for one request of the new member's model.

vectors.name: start-team-closed
vectors.description: The lead ended (a model failure), which closed the team. An operator start is refused team_closed after the team's grant.

vectors.name: start-operator
vectors.description: team.start: operator_request, the grant, member_started in the team log (its parent is the lead's thread_started, which carries the team; its provenance is the request) and the task from {operator: request_id}. The task monitor's watcher is the team log.

vectors.name: start-dynamic-defaults
vectors.description: No chosen field: member_started.define holds every choosable tool of the template, in its pinned order, and its first model key; no instructions.

vectors.name: start-dynamic-chosen
vectors.description: The lead chose a label, instructions, two tools and the strong model: member_started records define (tools in the template's order) and the label.

args.label: invoice checker
args.instructions: Look up the invoice and answer yes or no with its status.

vectors.name: start-dynamic-tool-not-allowed
vectors.description: A tool outside the template's choosable set: refused invalid_definition, whose detail lists the choosable tools so the model can correct itself. Nothing else is appended.

vectors.name: start-dynamic-choose-framework-tool
vectors.description: send is in the framework set F: every member keeps it and none chooses it.

vectors.name: start-dynamic-instructions-delimiter
vectors.description: Written text that closes the block with a fullwidth look-alike is refused invalid.

vectors.name: start-label-operator
vectors.description: operator is reserved: a from="operator" block always means an operator start.

vectors.name: start-static-with-define
vectors.description: researcher is a static agent: instructions on its start is not_allowed.

vectors.name: start-static-with-label
vectors.description: A label works on any start: researcher-2 starts with it on member_started.

vectors.name: start-dynamic-budget-headroom-strong-refused
vectors.description: The define is valid, but no budget has room for one request of the chosen model: budget_exceeded, checked after the definition.

vectors.name: materialize-opens-branch
vectors.description: The first consume of a starting member opens its branch: thread_started (the parent member_started names) and user_input{team_task} with the task, which consumes the task row; the row becomes running with its branch.

vectors.name: materialize-not-starting
vectors.description: The row check in the transaction: the member already has its branch and is no longer starting, so nothing is committed. This is also why branch.open's already_open never follows a passed row check.

vectors.name: failed-rebind-pin-unavailable
vectors.description: The rebind finds the definition unregistered: one append opens the branch with thread_started, the task's user_input, turn_completed{error: pin_unavailable} and member_ended{failed}; one member_ended notification for the lead's task monitor; then a mail_refused and a bounce per pending mail in (created_at, mail_id) order. Each log has its own clock here, so the writer's ask comes before the lead's message. The ask's bounce carries the ask_id and the result; each bounce carries its refused mail's provenance.

vectors.name: failed-rebind-pin-mismatch-fires-every-monitor
vectors.description: The rebuilt config_hash differs: the same end append, with one member_ended notification per monitor row on the member (the task monitor and the lead's end monitor), in monitor_id order.

vectors.name: failed-rebind-with-queued-cancel-and-wait
vectors.description: While researcher-1 was starting, the lead requested its cancel and writer-1 waits on it. The failed rebind fires the lead's task monitor and the writer's settle monitor (member_ended, monitor_id order), and returns the queued cancel with a bounce.

vectors.name: failed-rebind-bounce-keeps-its-request
vectors.description: Bob's operator request started writer-1, and Alice's lead run sent it a message. The rebind fails: the task notification (to the team log) carries Bob's provenance, but the bounce to the lead carries the message's, Alice's run, so it can't wake the lead under Bob's authority or budget root.

vectors.name: idle-fires-settle-and-task-monitors
vectors.description: The researcher's task turn ends completed: turn_completed, member_idle with the answer, then member_settled for each settle monitor and its unfired task monitor, in monitor_id order, deleting both rows; the row becomes idle with its result.

vectors.name: idle-after-wait-finished-sends-no-settle
vectors.description: The tie rule's loser: the lead's wait finished at its deadline first and deleted its settle row, so the researcher's later idle append sends only the task notification.

vectors.name: end-member-refuses-pending-mail
vectors.description: The researcher's model fails: turn_completed, member_ended{failed}, the task monitor's member_ended, then a mail_refused and a bounce for each pending mail (the writer's ask's bounce carries its ask_id and the result).

vectors.name: end-asker-closes-its-open-asks
vectors.description: The writer ends while its ask to researcher-1 is open: the same append closes the ask cancelled before member_ended, so no ask row outlives its asker; a later reply is refused ask_closed.

vectors.name: end-lead-closes-team
vectors.description: The lead's model fails: its member_ended sets teams.closed_at, and the same append sends one cancel to each live member (running researcher-1, running writer-1), in name order, with the lead's run as provenance.

vectors.name: ended-lead-refuses-late-notice
vectors.description: The lead's end closed the team and cancelled researcher-1, whose own end then fired the lead's task monitor. Mail reaching a member that already ended is refused under its writer, never left pending: mail_refused{member_ended}, with no bounce for a notification (only a message or an ask is bounced).

vectors.name: team-log-takes-park-notice
vectors.description: writer-1, started by the operator, parks on an ask; its member_parked notice goes to the team log, which records the receipt only: no parked, no turn.

vectors.name: team-log-takes-settlement
vectors.description: writer-1's settlement reaches the team log as its task notification: receipt only, no resumed and no turn.

vectors.name: team-log-takes-bounce
vectors.description: The operator's message to a starting member is returned when its rebind fails: the bounce reaches the team log, which records it.

vectors.name: team-log-wait-finishes
vectors.description: The operator waits for the running researcher; its idle append sends the settle mail to the team log, whose consume records it and finishes the wait (no resumed, no tool_result: team.wait returns it). The lead's task notification is not the team log's.

vectors.name: send-from-woken-turn
vectors.description: The lead's wake turn sends researcher-1 a message: the turn belongs to the run that spawned the woken child, so the message carries that run's principal and root request (the lead's user_input), exactly as a send in the run's first turn would.

vectors.name: start-from-woken-turn
vectors.description: The lead's wake turn starts researcher-2: member_started and its task carry the spawning run's provenance, so the new member belongs to that run.

vectors.name: wait-registers-monitor
vectors.description: The lead waits for a running member: the grant (wait is decided as monitor), wait_started (mode all, deadline now + 120 s) with a settle monitor row, and the park on the wait.

vectors.name: wait-already-settled
vectors.description: The researcher is already idle and is listed twice: the repeat is dropped before anything is recorded, wait_started lists it once, member_observed copies its committed member_idle result (source is that event), and the mode is met, so wait_finished and the call's result are in the same append. No park, no monitor row left.

vectors.name: wait-unknown-member-refused
vectors.description: A listed name is not a member: refused unknown_member before the policy is asked, recorded as the call's result.

vectors.name: wait-deadline-timed-out
vectors.description: The deadline step with the member still running: wait_finished{timed_out} lists it pending and deletes the monitor row; resumed and the call's result follow.

vectors.name: wait-deadline-counts-committed-settlement
vectors.description: The tie rule: the researcher's idle append deleted the settle monitor row and sent its notification before the deadline step ran, so the step consumes it and the member counts; the mode is met and timed_out is false. Commit order, never timestamps.

vectors.name: wait-operator-n-over-count-invalid
vectors.description: team.wait with mode 3 on two members is refused invalid_request before any writer is acquired: nothing is recorded, no request exists, and no row changes.

vectors.name: wait-operator-observed
vectors.description: team.wait on an idle member: operator_request, the grant, wait_started, member_observed and wait_finished in one append. The team log parks nothing.

vectors.name: wait-operator-any
vectors.description: team.wait mode any: the idle researcher is observed and meets the mode, so the wait finishes at once with the writer pending; any never cancels the others.

vectors.name: wait-deadline-lists-parked
vectors.description: The operator's wait on writer-1 reaches its deadline while the writer is parked on its ask: a parked member does not settle, so wait_finished lists it under parked and times out. The team log writes only wait_finished.

vectors.name: monitor-running
vectors.description: The lead monitors a running member: the grant, monitor_set and an end monitor row.

vectors.name: monitor-ended
vectors.description: The target already ended: monitor_set, then member_observed with its member_ended result, and the result says ended; no row.

vectors.name: monitor-unknown-member-refused
vectors.description: The grant is decided first, then the target is looked up: refused unknown_member.
